The sky is blue due to a phenomenon called **Rayleigh scattering**. 

Sunlight may appear white, but it's actually made up of all the colors of the rainbow. When this light reaches Earth's atmosphere, it collides with gas molecules (mostly nitrogen and oxygen). These molecules are much smaller than the wavelengths of visible light, so they scatter shorter wavelengths (blue and violet) much more efficiently than longer wavelengths (red, yellow).
